news.tick: +25bp to 3.75-4.00% · UNANIMOUS · dot plot 1+ more · ~42% odds of two · Dow -631
news.h: The Fed Raises Rates for the First Time Since 2023 — a Unanimous Quarter-Point Hike to 3.75-4.00%, With the Dot Plot Penciling In at Least One More This Year
news.body: In a UNANIMOUS vote, the FOMC raised the fed funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% — the first increase since 2023 and the first tightening of the Warsh era. The dot plot's median expects at least one more 2026 hike; futures price ~42% odds of two by year-end. Warsh: 'Productivity growth is strong and capital investment is robust, job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little. But inflation remains elevated. Today's policy action will support a timelier return to the committee's 2% goal.' 'Our predominant focus is on the price stability side of our mandate.' All three indexes were higher before the decision, then sold the presser — the Dow lost 631 points (-1.21%) to 51,461.90 with Goldman Sachs leading it lower; the S&P fell 0.45% to 7,551.81; the Nasdaq slipped 0.01% to 25,978.42. Trump blasted the hike ('rates should be 1%, or less') but avoided attacking Warsh. Higher yields raise net interest on the $40.1T national debt.
news.impact: The regime is now officially tightening. (1) A unanimous vote — doves included — means no dovish faction to bet on near-term; (2) 'one more' plus the market's '42% for two' makes December live; (3) Goldman leading the Dow lower on hike day is the growth reflex, before the NIM benefit shows in earnings. The hike validates every rate-sensitive trim (VST out) and the barbell. The question: does AI-driven growth keep outrunning the hikes? Catalyst's David Miller: 'As long as the growth keeps up to more than offset the rate hikes, you can still see equities continue to rally.'

news.tag: ⚠️ WHAT FORCED IT: HOT CPI + $100 OIL
news.h: The Hot August CPI and Oil Above $100 Left the Fed No Choice — the 10-Year Hit 4.95%, Its Highest Since October 2023, as the Market Fell Four Straight Days Into the Print
news.body: Thursday Sep 10: PPI was 'inconclusive' (21shares' Coltman) but oil surged — WTI closed $102.48 (+6.7%), Brent $107.63 (+5.9%), the highest closes since May 19, as the war stretched into its seventh month. WTI is up 52.9% since the war began and 78.5% YTD. The spike pushed the 10-year above 4.95% (highest since Oct 2023); the Treasury bought back $5.19B of long bonds to manage the curve. The S&P fell 0.58% to 7,591.70, a fourth straight decline; high-beta chips sold off on rate and oil fears. Friday Sep 11: August CPI came in HOT — headline +0.4% MoM, 3.4% YoY, core +0.3% MoM — and hike odds went above 90%.
news.impact: The Iran→oil→inflation→rates transmission ran to completion. (1) Core +0.3% MoM (~3.6% annualized) removed the doves' last argument; (2) WTI +78.5% YTD is the single biggest macro fact of 2026 — it explains the hike, the bond rout, and energy's +21% Q3; (3) A 4.95% 10Y is the highest since 2023 — the risk-free hurdle rose again. The CVX/energy leg of the dividend sleeve is the clear winner of this stretch; the Oct 13 CPI stays pivotal for December.

news.tick: Summit in Washington · oil holds losses · Goldman: 'moment of maximum leverage'
news.h: A Trump-Xi Summit in Washington This Week Adds a Fresh Catalyst — Markets Rise on the Talks, and Goldman Calls It 'the Moment of Maximum Leverage' for an Iran Deal
news.body: Presidents Trump and Xi meet in Washington later this week; futures edged higher and oil held losses as traders awaited details. The Iran dimension is key: Bessent's 'Operation Economic Outcast' secondary sanctions explicitly implicated China (Iran's primary oil buyer), so US-China cooperation is directly linked to an Iran resolution. CNBC: 'any sharp escalation that costs the U.S. a key intermediary in its war with Iran could exacerbate an energy crisis… potentially triggering a market correction. Any cooperation, however, could mean a sudden rush of relief.' Goldman's Rich Privorotsky: 'the economic incentive to de-escalate and find a deal is enormous. This is arguably the moment of maximum leverage for both sides.'
news.impact: A genuine two-way catalyst with an asymmetric bull case. (1) If China becomes an intermediary and oil breaks below $95, it unwinds the entire inflation→hike chain; (2) a breakdown is the correction scenario; (3) oil 'holding its losses' shows the market leaning hopeful. Keep the energy hedge as insurance, but a deal would hit energy hard and lift everything else — CVX is the one to trim into de-escalation.

news.h: The U.S.-Iran War Turns Kinetic Again — CENTCOM Strikes Iranian Targets, Two Tankers Hit at the Strait of Hormuz, Brent Tops $95
news.body: U.S. Central Command launched new attacks against Iranian targets after two oil tankers were struck exiting the Strait of Hormuz, sending Brent above $95. Global bond yields jumped as the hostilities reinforced inflation expectations and September hike bets.
news.impact: The worst-timed catalyst — an oil spike as the Fed weighs a hike. Energy gets a war bid, gold's haven role reactivates, and the risk to the broad market is real if oil holds above $95.

news.h: A Worldwide Government Bond Sell-Off Intensifies — the 10-Year Hits 4.79%, Its Highest Since January 2025
news.body: The 10-year rose to 4.79%, its highest since January 2025; the 30-year ~5.27%. Eurozone inflation hit 3.3%. Drivers compound: Iran-oil, Warsh's hawkish turn, US debt/supply, and the war re-escalation.
news.impact: Rising long yields compress multiples — especially rate-sensitive sectors. The bond rout reinforces the barbell: banks, short-duration quality, gold; avoid long duration.
